text:
incident-bot: Auto-detect: Inference latency P99 breach in eu-south-1a for several endpoints. Alert rule: p99 > 2.5s or error-rate > 0.7% -> sev2

aws-alerts: AWS advisory: elevated ENI attach failures and EC2 API throttling observed in eu-south-1a. See CloudTrail snippets and alarm: https://console.aws/alerts?id=atc-998877

Maya: Notifying oncall. I'll start collecting customer impact and flag any high-SLA customers.

Eli (oncall): oncall Eli here — acknowledging. Paging SRE + infra. @Sven @Priya join please. I'll start coordinating mitigations.

Sven (sre): Looking at NLB target statuses — a lot of our instances in eu-south-1a are cycling Unhealthy -> Initial -> Unhealthy. Health check latency increased and connection resets seen. ENI attach errors in control plane logs.

Noah (runtime): Runtime logs show many in-flight KV cache population goroutines hitting econnreset when talking to local key-value frontends. We see backpressure: worker queue depth increasing and batch latency spikes. Impacted models: rwd-llama-7b, rwd-chat-2.

Priya (infra): Correlating with AWS: they reported underlying host maintenance and subsequent capacity rebalancing in the AZ causing attach/attach-ENI rate limiting on our account. Also one of our resolver DaemonSets restarted in the AZ during the maintenance - likely left some pods using stale resolver endpoints.

Eli (oncall): Quick mitigation plan — short term: 1) mark eu-south-1a as degraded in routing. 2) drain NLB targets in that AZ. 3) reduce internal DNS caching TTLs and evict resolver entries. 4) scale fallback capacity in eu-west-3 and eu-central-1. 5) reduce inference batch sizes for fallback pools to keep tail latency low.

eng-ops-bot: Applying playbook steps:
```
# mark AZ degraded
redwood routing set-az-status --region eu-south-1 --az a --status degraded --reason "eni-throttling"
# force-deregister targets
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --targets Id=i-aaaa --region eu-south-1
# lower resolver TTL
redwood infra dns update --zone internal --record resolver.eu-south-1 --ttl 8
# scale fallback
redwood infra scale --region eu-west-3 --pool inference-gpu --add 8
```

Sven (sre): Force-deregister started — but NLB still shows some inflight connections are sticky; pushing to terminate long-lived connections. Also toggling connection draining timeout to 10s to accelerate failover.

Noah (runtime): Spinning up warm replicas in eu-west-3 and priming KV cache with hottest prefixes. Also toggling runtime to lower batch size from 32->8 for fallback nodes to reduce p99.

incident-bot: Automated routing adjustment: 65% of new requests now avoid eu-south-1a, 35% still allowed for safe-canary traffic while caches warm.

Priya (infra): Confirmed with AWS support: API throttles are from internal attach quotas due to host maintenance. They recommended moving traffic away from AZ and not repeatedly retrying attaches. They've opened a ticket to monitor host stabilization.

Maya: Customer status: 7 customers reported slow responses or intermittent 5xx. One enterprise account reported broadly elevated latencies and requested SLA investigation. CS sent immediate notification templates and offered targeted reroute assistance.

Eli (oncall): Added mitigation: update client SDK sticky-host TTLs (client side) to 15s for affected regions so clients re-resolve faster. Also enable HTTP/1.1 connection close on our edge for new connections to avoid long-lived sticky sockets.

Noah (runtime): After initial fallback, kvcache populate p99 dropped from ~3.1s -> 1.0s for traffic hitting eu-west-3 warm replicas. Error-rate on fallback nodes stable < 0.2%.

eng-ops-bot: DNS TTL change applied for resolver records (ttl=8s) — propagation in progress.

Priya (infra): Rolling restart of resolver pods in eu-south-1a performed to clear stuck state. We will keep a small number of resolvers up to avoid total loss while AWS stabilizes.

Sven (sre): Observing ENI attach Throttling errors in control-plane logs. Sample:
```
2029-08-03T14:02:12Z AttachNetworkInterface Throttling: Rate exceeded AttachNetworkInterface
status code: 400
```

Maya: CS has compiled list of impacted customers and mitigation statuses; enterprise customers notified of potential SLA impact and assigned CS leads.

Eli (oncall): Handoff notes to next oncall (Sven): cause = AWS AZ host rebalancing + resolver pod restart -> control-plane ENI attach throttles + sticky connections -> p99 latency and 5xx. Actions taken = AZ marked degraded, NLB targets drained, client sticky TTLs lowered, DNS TTL lowered, resolvers rolled, fallback capacity launched in eu-west-3 & eu-central-1, batches reduced on fallback. Customer comms sent.

Sven (sre): Taking over. I will monitor ENI attach success rate, NLB health transitions, resolver latency, and fallback traffic split. If AWS doesn't mark AZ stable in 45 minutes, we'll escalate with account team and consider temporary long-term traffic shift. Updating incident to sev2 and adding to postmortem queue.

eng-ops-bot: Handoff recorded. Next update scheduled in 15m.
